title: New Tour Takes Visitors Inside Japan's Northern Alps
paragraphs: Pack your camera — and get ready to put on a hard hat. A new sightseeing route in Japan takes visitors deep inside the Northern Alps, where trains, tunnels and a power plant are hidden beneath the mountains.

The Kurobe-Unazuki Canyon Route opened on October 2 in Toyama prefecture. Stretching 18 kilometers, it connects Keyakidaira Station on the Kurobe Gorge Railway with Kurobe Dam on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route.
Visitors travel through tunnels built to carry workers and equipment for power plant construction, switching between five types of transport.
From Keyakidaira, a small train takes visitors into the mountain. Then comes an elevator ride: 200 meters straight up through the rock.

Next, visitors board a battery-powered train — and things soon heat up! The train passes through the "high-temperature tunnel," where temperatures reach around 40 degrees Celsius. During construction in the 1930s, workers encountered rock as hot as 160 degrees!
At the end of the railway is the Kurobe River No. 4 Power Plant, which uses water from Kurobe Dam to generate electricity. Completed in 1963, it was built underground to protect the landscape above.

A cable car then climbs a steep underground track, taking passengers about 450 meters higher. From there, a 40-minute bus journey takes them toward the dam — with a chance to get the camera out as the bus stops to let visitors walk through a side tunnel to a mountain viewpoint overlooking the surrounding peaks.
Tour guide Masami Amano told Kyodo News this view is her favorite part of the trip.
"It's an opportunity to view scenery that most people never will. Even experienced hikers have difficulty reaching these locations," she said.

Because the route remains a working industrial site, visitors must travel with a guide. Packages sold through Japanese travel companies include a night's stay in Toyama City, Unazuki Onsen in Toyama prefecture, or Omachi Onsen Village in Nagano.
This year's tours run until November 30.
